newsitem.title: UK: UK government calls conference on water issues.
newsitem.headline: UK government calls conference on water issues.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government said on Tuesday it will hold a summit on water resource problems on May 19 in London, where it will put forward plans for action to tackle drought problems.

"This government is determined to take decisive action to tackle the causes of the problems which the experience of the past few years and the current drought has highlighted," deputy prime minister John Prescott said in a statement.

Britain is suffering its worst drought for 200 years while water companies have been under heavy criticism for the amount of water leaking out of pipes, which some estimates put at over 800 million gallons a day.
The conference will be held at the Queen Elizabeth II centre in central London.

"Climate change and household growth are likely to put increasing pressure on water use. We need to take action now to ensure that everyone is playing their full part," added Prescott, who counts the environment among his varied responsibilities.
Water companies, industry regulator Ofwat, the Environment Agency, environmental and consumer groups have all been invited to attend the conference.
The privatised water companies have been fiercely criticised by Labour and lobby groups for paying out hefty dividends and executive pay packets while struggling to meet demand during the drought.

The government intends to impose a one-off "windfall" tax on it has described as the "excess profits" of privatised utilities in order to finance a three billion pound ($4.9 billion) plan to put young and long-term unemployed people to work.
Next week's water conference will tackle leakage and efficiency as well as licensing companies to take water from rivers.
"The idea is that the government will see this as the first step to start some action," an environment department spokesman said.
"We want to see the companies getting together more with customers...everyone involved can develop their own ways of saving water," he added.
Prescott will make a speech to the conference, which will be chaired by environment minister Michael Meacher.
